question: What initializes and writes the 33 mutable wonder slots consumed by the city production menu?

scope.boundary: This packet identifies one reset and one completion-path writer for 33 slots. It does not prove when the reset runs, save/load parity, all table writers, actual runtime slot values, global wonder validity, or construction effects.

dependencies.use: Establishes the 33-slot -1 test and 200 through 232 menu output range.
Establishes the 0 through 32 helper entry guard and city-update mode-one call.
Separates 37 initialized definition identities from this 33-slot state table.

reset.action: Inside 0x82D05D50, r3 receives table base 0x830E5148, r4 receives -1, and r5 receives 0x108 bytes before direct call to 0x827F7BB0. This sets all bytes of the 33 eight-byte slots to 0xFF on that path.
reset.qualification: The image's zero-filled bytes are pre-runtime content. This call establishes a static reset path; its execution timing and live values were not observed.

claimWrite.guard: 0x82D16BA0 branches out for a negative normalized wonder index or index at least 33. Its mode-one bit test at 0x82D16BE0 guards the slot stores.
claimWrite.fields: At 0x82D16BF4 index*8 selects a slot. 0x82D16C08 writes the city's signed owner byte to first word +0x00. 0x82D16C10 writes incoming city index r4 to second word +0x04. The helper then calls 0x82D00480 with an owner/index-derived value; that call's meaning is outside this packet.
claimWrite.qualification: The accepted city-update caller reaches this helper only after sufficient production and the separate nonzero eligibility gate. These are static writes; no wonder construction or effect was observed at runtime.

menuUse: At 0x82CE3038 through 0x82CE3040 the menu generator loads slot first word and compares it with -1, then calls 0x82CF3608 only when it matches. The reset and mode-one writer provide a local unclaimed/claimed interpretation for this equality; other writers and restored state remain unclassified.

currentEvidence.method: Foreground read-only Ghidra exact raw-word and capped split-constant scans against the pinned image, followed by narrow generated-code corroboration of exact reset and helper windows where Ghidra lacks containing functions.

guards: Do not infer live -1 values solely from image zeros or the presence of a reset call.
Do not equate the 33-slot table with the 37 initialized wonder definitions.
Do not assign save/load, other writer, effect, or multiplayer ownership semantics from these two local paths.

nextObservation.authorization: Plan only. A new Title runtime probe requires separate user authorization and must not be run from this Research task without it.
nextObservation.placement: Default-off, one-menu probe at 0x82CE3034 before each slot read and 0x82CE3050 immediately after the 0x82CF3608 eligibility call. No other hooks are needed for this discriminator.
nextObservation.requiredFields: For each first-hook event log normalized index r30, city byte-offset r25, both words at slot pointer r31, and a per-invocation marker. For each second-hook event log r30 and returned r3, with the same marker. Record at most one complete 33-index menu pass and at most 33 post-call results; do not sample other gameplay.
nextObservation.stopCondition: The owner opens one city's wonder choices and exits normally. A complete pass includes exactly normalized indices 0 through 32; correlate each -1 first-word slot with the second-hook return to establish which IDs this menu admitted in that state. Any incomplete pass remains inconclusive. This still does not test IDs 233 through 236, which this menu never enumerates.

conclusion: The city wonder menu's -1 slot test has an explicit 0x108-byte all-FF reset path and an accepted 0-through-32 mode-one completion-path writer that stores owner and city index in the same slots. The exact runtime table contents, save/load handling, and other consumers remain unresolved.
